about: avenDB's performance gates, held by scripts/ci/avendb-bench.mjs to the lines of crates/avendb/tests/bench_gates.rs and crates/avendb-server/tests/relay_bench.rs (the bench job of avendb-checks.yml). A gate missed fails the PR; a target is printed with whether it is met. Gates sit at the level reached on 2026-10-27 with headroom for a shared runner; raise one when the code reaches past it. The carriers' gates sit at under half of the first CI run's (2026-10-27: direct 582 edits/s, relay 710, a 1 MB/s link 93 edits/s at 0.56 of it, 1001 edits of 6 KB); draft_on_ratio_max (1.2) is null until Log::draft_on reads its log's index (claude/s-draft-on). The phone-class rows (WebAssembly in Chromium and WebKit) gate nothing yet. The index rows (index_sizes, parity_n: avendb-net's shelf_index_bench.rs, run with --index in the net test shard) gate counts, not only time: a view opened cold steps on no log edit and reads pages as the tree is deep (depth within the model's; a view's 50 rows the median open reads at most one page past the depth, the worst of 200 at most 6, as a page may hold few rows); 2026-10-27: 1M 3 deep, at most 7 pages, 81 KB; 10M 4, 8, 59 KB; 100M (by hand) 4, 7, 67 KB, built in 157 s; 49 index bytes/edit at each. The window rows (window_sizes: avendb-net's query_window_bench.rs, gate G1 of batch 5) answer a named query end to end as Node::windowed does (query_window::answer: the window off the shared index, then the query over its entries), cold, at 1M and 10M edits: 2026-10-27 (views lane 37fd1fd, stamp checked by of_log), 1M 3 pages median, 4 at most, 49 KB, 50 rows, 0 log edits, 4.3 ms p50; 10M 3, 4, 66 KB, 4.8 ms (debug; the index part is about 0.1 ms, the rest the query's 50 rows); its growth from 1M to 10M is gated (1.12 then). The log's head a node works out once as it opens is a target: 322 ms at 1M, 3.4 s at 10M. The posts row (avendb-net's posts_page_bench.rs, run with --posts in the net test shard) holds a page of the Universe's posts on a node, off the shared index, as the always-on peer's /feed/posts and Node::run serve it: no more per edit of a post (it reads no history) and under 5 ms at 1M and 10M edits, from the slopes measured on small vaults. The engine's own walk (2026-10-27: 6.2 µs per edit of a post, 4.4 per entry held, 96 ms at 1M) is no longer on any served path (primitives lane 09d93b4); 2026-10-28 on the node: 0.6 ms a page at 1M and 10M, 0.2 µs per edit of a post. log_bytes_per_edit_max (3,585 on 2026-10-27: 244 bytes an edit, its id, one ML-DSA-65 signature an edit while S8 is off) catches growth; the target bytes_ratio_pg (log over Postgres's bytes/edit) needs S8's one signature a segment. The live rows (live_links: avendb-net's tests/sync_bench.rs, plan D3, batch 5's exit gates) hold a live edit's delay while a device catches up on a bulk of history, on a simulated calm link and a phone's (50 Mbit/s, 40 ms round trip, 1 % lost): p95 under 500 ms, none missing at 15 s, the catch-up using at least 80 % of a set-rate link, and at most 5 % of edits sent again. First run, 2026-10-27, calm, 3,000 edits: catch-up 14 s (215 edits/s), live p95 11.8 s during it (the iPhone's LIVE_WAIT case), 107 ms idle. The live shard builds with --profile live and --cfg avendb_no_replay_checks (no whole-log replay on each write; the debug build timed itself, phone_bulk 60 s). A live edit is written every 100 ms during a catch-up, and the phone_bulk run must time at least 40, so its p95 is no max; the live-delay gates hold every run. 2026-10-28 on the batch head (vjjtfj ecd7383): phone_bulk 13 s, 0.28 of the link, 16 % sent again, live p95 3.0 s (with a live edit every 250 ms instead: 5.7 s, 0.64, 4.6 %, 212 ms, so live writes slow the catch-up); phone 600 edits 1.5 s, p95 720 ms; calm 0.7 s, p95 534 ms; calm_bulk 0.7 s. The link's use (G3) is held on the _bulk runs alone, 20 MB of 48 KB edits each an entry of its own, so the wire's time and not the receiver's cost per edit is most of the catch-up (the 600-edit runs, kept for G4's live delay, sync in under a second on a calm link against 0.58 s of wire): calm_bulk is the control. The writes row (avendb-net's lab_schedule_bench.rs, G5, in the live shard) holds a person's write while a 20 ms catch-up slice runs and 32 reads of 20 ms wait: ahead of every queued read, p95 under 50 ms (2026-10-28: p50 26, p95 31, max 34 ms).

vs_main.about: Each gate's value is also held against main's build, timed on the same runner in the same job, the two taking turns (scripts/ci/avendb-bench-shard.mjs; Goal 6 D3, Samuel 2026-10-28): no worse than main's by more than this share of main's value. The fixed gates above hold too.
vs_main.gate_about: Printed, not failing, until the timed benches give the same numbers run after run (2026-10-28, 5 rounds each on one runner, the branch's code the same as main's: phone_bulk's catch-up used 0.227 to 0.489 of its link, median 0.342 against main's 0.475, and phone's idle p95 came out 31 % apart, so a 15 % gate failed identical code). A stage, not the end: vs_main turns on once phone_bulk is deterministic (seeded loss and simulated time on the phone link, the bench lane's item 2 of Goal 6), so the same code gives the same number. The fixed gates fail as before.
